Details: 1-Data Abstraction.webm: A lecture recording introducing data abstraction, focusing on abstract data types, compound data, and the implementation of rational numbers as an example. | 2-Representing Rational Numbers.mkv: A lecture segment introducing the representation of rational numbers using lists in Python, covering pairs, list operations, and the importance of data abstraction and normalization (lowest terms) for rational numbers. | 3-Abstraction Barriers.mkv: A lecture segment discussing abstraction barriers in programming, using the example of rational arithmetic systems, and illustrating the consequences of violating these barriers with code examples. | 4-Data Representations.mkv: A lecture segment discussing data abstraction, focusing on abstraction barriers, data representation, and implementing rational numbers using both lists and functions. | 5-Trees.mkv: A lecture recording introducing the tree data abstraction, covering tree vocabulary, recursive structure, and implementation details in Python, including constructors, selectors, and abstraction barriers. | 6-Tree Processing.mkv: A lecture recording on tree processing in computer programs, focusing on tree recursion, constructing and traversing trees, and implementing functions to manipulate tree structures such as counting leaves, extracting leaf labels, and incrementing tree values. | 7-Example： Printing Trees.mkv: A lecture segment demonstrating how to write and improve a tree-printing function in Python, focusing on visualizing tree structures using indentation to reflect depth. | 8-Example： Summing Paths.mkv: A lecture recording demonstrating recursive strategies for summing values along paths in trees, contrasting return-value-based and argument-passing recursion, with examples using factorial and tree traversal. | 9-Example： Counting Paths.mkv: A lecture segment introducing a recursive problem: counting the number of paths in a tree whose node labels sum to a given total, including detailed discussion of problem analysis and recursive solution structure.

name: Mutability (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Objects.webm, 2-Example： Strings.mkv, 3-Mutation Operations.webm, 4-Tuples.webm, 5-Mutation.mkv, 6-Mutable Functions.mkv, 7-Examples： Lists.webm. Details: 1-Objects.webm: A lecture segment introducing the concept of objects in software engineering, focusing on Python's object system, classes, attributes, methods, and the object-oriented programming paradigm. | 2-Example： Strings.mkv: A lecture recording introducing strings in programming, focusing on string methods, character encoding (ASCII and Unicode), and how text is represented and manipulated in Python and other languages. | 3-Mutation Operations.webm: A lecture recording introducing mutation operations in Python, focusing on how objects like lists and dictionaries can change their contents over time, with examples from playing cards and function calls. | 4-Tuples.webm: A lecture video introducing tuples in Python, focusing on their immutability, syntax, use cases, and differences from lists, as well as implications for dictionary keys and mutation. | 5-Mutation.mkv: A lecture segment on mutation in programming, discussing object identity, equality, and the dangers of mutable default arguments in functions. | 6-Mutable Functions.mkv: A lecture segment explaining mutable functions in Python, focusing on how mutable values enable functions to maintain and update persistent local state, using a bank account withdrawal example. | 7-Examples： Lists.webm: A lecture video on list mutation and environment diagrams, covering how list operations like append, extend, addition, slicing, pop, remove, and slice assignment affect list contents and variable bindings in Python.

name: Mutable Trees (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Tree Class.mkv, 2-Tree Mutation.mkv. Details: 1-Tree Class.mkv: A lecture recording introducing the tree data structure, comparing it to linked lists, and demonstrating tree implementation and processing in Python using both data abstraction and object-oriented approaches. | 2-Tree Mutation.mkv: A lecture segment on tree mutation, specifically focusing on pruning subtrees from a tree data structure by modifying its branches in place.

name: Objects and Attributes (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Object-Oriented Programming.mkv, 2-Class Statements.mkv, 3-Creating Instances.mkv, 4-Methods.mkv, 5-Method Calls.mkv, 6-Attribute Lookup.mkv, 7-Class Attributes.mkv, 8-Bound Methods.mkv, 9-Attribute Assignment.mkv. Details: 1-Object-Oriented Programming.mkv: A lecture recording introducing object-oriented programming, focusing on its principles, terminology, and how Python implements classes, objects, and methods. | 2-Class Statements.mkv: A lecture segment introducing class statements in Python, focusing on defining custom classes, instance attributes, and methods using a bank account example. | 3-Creating Instances.mkv: A lecture segment on object-oriented programming in Python, focusing on how instances are created, how attributes are assigned and accessed, and the concept of object identity. | 4-Methods.mkv: A lecture segment explaining method definitions in Python classes, focusing on how methods access object state via 'self', the use of dot notation, and the rationale for defining class-specific methods. | 5-Method Calls.mkv: A lecture segment explaining method calls in Python, focusing on dot notation, bound methods, and practical examples using an Account class. | 6-Attribute Lookup.mkv: A lecture segment explaining attribute lookup in Python objects, covering the evaluation of dot expressions, the search order for attributes, and the use of built-in functions like getattr and hasattr. | 7-Class Attributes.mkv: A lecture segment explaining class attributes in Python, focusing on how they are created, their behavior, and their distinction from instance attributes. | 8-Bound Methods.mkv: A lecture segment explaining Python's bound methods, class and instance attributes, and the distinction between functions and bound methods in object-oriented programming. | 9-Attribute Assignment.mkv: A lecture segment explaining attribute assignment in Python classes and instances, focusing on how assignments affect class and instance attributes, with illustrative examples using an Account class.

name: Recursion
description: Folder containing: 1-Self-Reference.webm, 2-Recursive Functions.mkv, 3-Recursion in Environment Diagrams.mkv, 4-Verifying Recursive Functions.mkv, 5-Mutual Recursion.mkv, 6-Recursion and Iteration.mkv. Details: 1-Self-Reference.webm: A lecture segment discussing self-reference in functions, focusing on how functions can refer to themselves and use inner functions to accumulate state across calls. | 2-Recursive Functions.mkv: A lecture recording introducing recursive functions, focusing on their definition, real-world examples, and a step-by-step implementation for summing the digits of a number using recursion. | 3-Recursion in Environment Diagrams.mkv: A lecture recording discussing recursion in environment diagrams, focusing on the factorial function, the mechanics of recursive calls, and a comparison between recursive and iterative implementations. | 4-Verifying Recursive Functions.mkv: A lecture segment discussing how to verify the correctness of recursive functions, focusing on the recursive leap of faith, base cases, and functional abstraction using the factorial example. | 5-Mutual Recursion.mkv: A lecture segment explaining mutual recursion, using the Luhn algorithm for credit card checksums as a practical example, including step-by-step computation and implementation details. | 6-Recursion and Iteration.mkv: A lecture segment discussing the relationship between recursion and iteration, focusing on how to convert recursive functions to iterative implementations and vice versa, using the sumDigits example.

name: SQL and Tables (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Databases.webm, 2-Structured Query Language.webm, 3-Projecting Tables.webm, 4-Arithmetic.mkv, 5-Joining Tables.webm, 6-Aliases & Dot Expressions.webm, 7-Numerical Expressions.mkv, 8-String Expressions.webm. Details: 1-Databases.webm: A lecture video introducing databases, focusing on database management systems, table structures, and the declarative nature of SQL compared to imperative programming languages. | 2-Structured Query Language.webm: A lecture video introducing the basics of SQL, focusing on installation, basic usage with SQLite, SELECT statements, and table creation using CREATE TABLE and UNION. | 3-Projecting Tables.webm: A lecture recording on projecting tables in SQL, focusing on how SELECT statements can create new tables from existing ones by specifying columns, filtering rows, and ordering results. | 4-Arithmetic.mkv: A lecture recording on SQL SELECT statements, focusing on arithmetic operations, row-wise computation, and declarative programming properties, with examples involving ski lift data and powers of two. | 5-Joining Tables.webm: A lecture recording on SQL joins, focusing on how to combine data from multiple tables using both implicit and explicit join syntax, with examples involving dog family trees and attributes. | 6-Aliases & Dot Expressions.webm: A lecture video on SQL joins, focusing on the use of aliases and dot expressions to disambiguate columns and tables, especially when joining a table with itself. The session covers practical examples involving parent-child and grandparent-grandchild relationships, and includes a multiple-choice assessment on constructing grandparent-grandchild queries. | 7-Numerical Expressions.mkv: A lecture segment introducing numerical expressions in SQL, comparing them to Python, and demonstrating their use in SELECT statements, including arithmetic operations, function calls, and table joins for calculating distances between cities. | 8-String Expressions.webm: A lecture segment on string expressions in SQL, focusing on string concatenation, basic string manipulation functions, and the use of strings to represent structured data, with practical examples of constructing sentences from database tables.

name: Scheme
description: Folder containing: 1-Scheme.webm, 2-Scheme Interpreters.mkv, 3-Special Forms.webm, 4-Lambda Expressions.mkv, 5-More Special Forms.mkv, 6-Example： Sierpinski's Triangle.mkv. Details: 1-Scheme.webm: An introductory lecture on the Scheme programming language, covering its historical context, syntax, core concepts, and basic usage, with comparisons to Python and an emphasis on the simplicity and beauty of Lisp dialects. | 2-Scheme Interpreters.mkv: A lecture segment explaining how Scheme code is executed, focusing on building and using a Scheme interpreter implemented in Python as part of a course project. | 3-Special Forms.webm: A lecture segment introducing Scheme's special forms, including 'if', 'and', 'or', and 'define', and demonstrating how to define procedures and recursive functions such as square root using these forms. | 4-Lambda Expressions.mkv: A lecture segment introducing lambda expressions in Scheme, focusing on their syntax, use for creating anonymous procedures, and their flexibility in procedure definition and application. | 5-More Special Forms.mkv: A lecture video introducing three Scheme special forms—cond, begin, and let—explaining their syntax, use cases, and differences from similar constructs in Python.

name: Scheme Lists
description: Folder containing: 1-Lists.mkv, 2-Symbolic Programming.mkv, 3-List Processing.webm, 4-Example： Even Subsets.mkv, 5-Discussion Question： Even Subsets Using Filter.mkv. Details: 1-Lists.mkv: A lecture video introducing Scheme's list data structures, comparing them to Python's linked lists, and demonstrating list construction, access, and built-in procedures in Scheme. | 2-Symbolic Programming.mkv: A lecture segment introducing symbolic programming in Lisp, focusing on the concept of quotation and its role in manipulating symbols and lists directly, with practical demonstrations and an assessment question on list operations. | 3-List Processing.webm: A lecture segment introducing and demonstrating built-in list processing procedures in Scheme, including append, map, filter, and apply, with practical examples and distinctions between their behaviors. | 4-Example： Even Subsets.mkv: A lecture segment on recursive list processing, focusing on defining a procedure to find all nonempty subsets of a list of integers whose sums are even, and refactoring the solution using higher-order functions. | 5-Discussion Question： Even Subsets Using Filter.mkv: A discussion video exploring how to generate all even-sum subsets of an integer list using filtering, including a breakdown of subset generation and the use of higher-order functions for filtering.

name: Sequences and Containers (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Lists.webm, 10-Strings.mkv, 11-Dictionaries.mkv, 2-Containers.mkv, 3-For Statements.mkv, 4-Ranges.mkv, 5-List Comprehensions.mkv, 6-Lists, Slices, & Recursion.mkv, 7-Box-and-Pointer Notation.webm, 8-Slicing.mkv, 9-Processing Container Values.mkv. Details: 1-Lists.webm: A lecture segment introducing Python lists, covering list creation, indexing, list operations, nested lists, and related built-in functions. | 10-Strings.mkv: A lecture segment introducing strings in Python, discussing their abstraction, representation, syntax, and sequence-like behaviors, with comparisons to other sequence types. | 11-Dictionaries.mkv: A lecture recording introducing Python dictionaries, covering their syntax, key-value structure, restrictions, dictionary comprehensions, and practical applications such as building index functions. | 2-Containers.mkv: A lecture segment introducing Python's 'in' and 'not in' operators for checking membership in containers, with examples and clarifications on how these operators work with lists and nested structures. | 3-For Statements.mkv: A lecture recording introducing the 'for' statement in Python, focusing on sequence iteration, assignment operators, and sequence unpacking within for loops. | 4-Ranges.mkv: A lecture recording introducing the concept of ranges in Python, explaining their properties, usage, and differences from lists, with practical examples and conventions for iteration. | 5-List Comprehensions.mkv: A lecture segment introducing list comprehensions in Python, demonstrating their syntax, use cases, and how they can be used to filter and transform lists, including within functions. | 6-Lists, Slices, & Recursion.mkv: A lecture video introducing lists, slicing, and recursion in Python, with examples of recursive list processing and tree recursion for sublist sum problems. | 7-Box-and-Pointer Notation.webm: A lecture segment explaining box and pointer notation for representing lists in environment diagrams, focusing on closure property, hierarchical structures, and how nested and compound values are depicted. | 8-Slicing.mkv: A lecture segment explaining the concept of slicing in Python, focusing on its syntax, behavior, and effects on lists and sequences. | 9-Processing Container Values.mkv: A lecture recording on processing container values in Python, focusing on built-in sequence aggregation functions such as sum, max, all, min, and any, including their usage, parameters, and behavior.

name: Tail Calls (Su25)
description: Folder containing: 1-Tail Recursion.webm, 2-Tail Calls.mkv, 3-Tail Recursion Examples.mkv, 4-Map and Reduce.mkv. Details: 1-Tail Recursion.webm: A lecture recording introducing tail recursion in the context of functional programming, comparing recursive and iterative approaches, and discussing the efficiency benefits of tail recursion in functional languages. | 2-Tail Calls.mkv: A lecture recording on tail calls in recursive procedures, covering the definition of tail contexts, the importance of tail call optimization for space efficiency, and practical demonstrations in Scheme and Python interpreters. | 3-Tail Recursion Examples.mkv: A lecture segment analyzing examples of tail recursion, focusing on identifying which recursive procedures are tail recursive and explaining the implications for space usage. | 4-Map and Reduce.mkv: A lecture segment introducing the higher-order functions 'map' and 'reduce', focusing on their definitions, recursive structure, and how to implement them efficiently with tail recursion.

name: Tree Recursion
description: Folder containing: 1-Order of Recursive Calls.webm, 2-Example： Inverse Cascade.mkv, 3-Tree Recursion.mkv, 4-Example： Counting Partitions.webm. Details: 1-Order of Recursive Calls.webm: A lecture recording discussing the order of recursive calls using the 'cascade' function as an example, covering base cases, recursive case structure, environment diagrams, and considerations for code clarity in recursive function design. | 2-Example： Inverse Cascade.mkv: A lecture segment introducing the concept of an inverse cascade, focusing on recursive function design using higher-order functions, specifically through the implementation of 'grow' and 'shrink' helper functions. | 3-Tree Recursion.mkv: A lecture recording explaining tree recursion, focusing on the Fibonacci sequence as a classic example, and analyzing the computational process, inefficiency, and tracing of recursive calls. | 4-Example： Counting Partitions.webm: A lecture video explaining the concept of counting integer partitions using tree recursion, including the recursive decomposition strategy, base cases, and a step-by-step walkthrough of the recursive process and its implementation.

name: [CS 61A SP24] Mega Discussion 08
description: Folder containing: 1-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #1 Strange Loop.mkv, 2-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #2 Sum Two Ways.mkv, 3-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Iterative).webm, 4-[CS61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #4 Overlap Growth.webm, 5-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Recursive).webm. Details: 1-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #1 Strange Loop.mkv: A discussion section walkthrough video for CS 61A, focusing on constructing a cyclic linked list (a 'strange loop') using the Link class, including diagramming, step-by-step construction, and handling cyclic references in code. | 2-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Problem #2 Sum Two Ways.mkv: A discussion walkthrough video for CS 61A, focusing on implementing sum functions for linked lists using both recursion and iteration, highlighting base and recursive cases, and iterative traversal. | 3-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Iterative).webm: A discussion video walkthrough for CS61A's 'overlap' problem, focusing on designing and implementing an iterative solution to count overlapping elements in two sorted linked lists. | 4-[CS61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #4 Overlap Growth.webm: A discussion video analyzing the runtime complexity of an alternative implementation of the 'overlap' function in CS61A, focusing on runtime analysis, composite function calls, and order of growth (constant, linear, quadratic, exponential). | 5-[CS 61A SP24] Discussion 8 Question #3 Overlap (Recursive).webm: A discussion video walkthrough for CS61A's 'overlap' problem, focusing on developing a recursive solution to count common elements in two sorted linked lists.

name: [CS 61A SU24 Discussion 2]
description: Folder containing: 1-Bottles.mkv, 2-Environment Diagrams： Assignment and Def Statements (Q7 & Q8).webm, 3-Digit Finder.mkv, 4-61A FA21 Disc02： Make Keeper.mkv, 5-Match Maker.mkv. Details: 1-Bottles.mkv: A lecture walkthrough on environment diagrams, focusing on how function calls create frames, variable assignment within frames, and the effects of local versus global variable assignment in Python. | 2-Environment Diagrams： Assignment and Def Statements (Q7 & Q8).webm: A lecture segment introducing environment diagrams in Python, focusing on assignment statements and def statements, including step-by-step procedures and binding rules. | 3-Digit Finder.mkv: A lecture recording explaining the implementation of a higher-order function to find the kth digit from the right in a number, covering digit manipulation techniques and edge cases. | 4-61A FA21 Disc02： Make Keeper.mkv: A discussion section walkthrough video for the 'makeKeeper' higher-order function problem, covering function definition, inner functions, parameter passing, and control flow in Python. | 5-Match Maker.mkv: A lecture walkthrough for the 'match k' function problem, focusing on digit manipulation without string conversion, using modular arithmetic and floor division to compare digits k apart in a number.

name: [CS 61A SU24] Discussion 01
description: Folder containing: 1-Race.mkv, 2-Fizzbuzz.mkv, 3-Is Prime.mkv, 4-Unique Digits.mkv, 5-Ordered Digits.mkv. Details: 1-Race.mkv: A walkthrough video explaining the implementation and analysis of a 'race' function, focusing on edge cases where the function returns incorrect results or runs indefinitely. | 2-Fizzbuzz.mkv: A lecture segment explaining the implementation of the FizzBuzz function, focusing on loop construction, conditional logic, and correct ordering of conditions. | 3-Is Prime.mkv: A solution walkthrough video for a discussion problem on implementing a recursive function to check if a number is prime, focusing on recursion, helper functions, and base cases. | 4-Unique Digits.mkv: A walkthrough video for the 'unique digits' programming problem, covering two algorithmic approaches to count unique digits in a positive integer using digit extraction and helper functions. | 5-Ordered Digits.mkv: A walkthrough video for Lab 3 of CS 61A, focusing on the 'ordered digits' problem. The video covers problem interpretation, human and algorithmic strategies, digit extraction techniques, and implementation logic for checking non-decreasing digit order in integers.

name: [CS 61A SU25] Discussion 3
description: Folder containing: 1-Question 1 - Recursive Multiplication.mkv, 2-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #2 Swipe.webm, 3-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #3 Skip Factorial.mkv, 4-Question 5 - Recursive Hailstone.mkv. Details: 1-Question 1 - Recursive Multiplication.mkv: A lecture recording discussing recursive multiplication, focusing on defining a multiplication function using recursion instead of the multiplication operator. | 2-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #2 Swipe.webm: A discussion section walkthrough for a recursion problem, focusing on implementing a function to print digits of a number backwards and then forwards without using iteration. | 3-[CS 61A SU24] Discussion 3 Problem #3 Skip Factorial.mkv: A discussion walkthrough for a recursion problem, specifically focusing on defining the base case for a skip factorial function and analyzing recursive structure and test cases. | 4-Question 5 - Recursive Hailstone.mkv: A video walkthrough for a programming question on implementing the Hailstone sequence recursively, covering base cases, recursive cases, and the relationship between iterative and recursive solutions.

name: [CS 61A SU25] Discussion 6
description: Folder containing: 1-Keyboard.webm, 2-Shapes.mkv, 3-Bear.webm. Details: 1-Keyboard.webm: A lecture walkthrough of the 'keyboard problem', focusing on the design and implementation of interacting classes: CapsLock, Button, and Keyboard, including their attributes, methods, and how they work together to simulate keyboard behavior. | 2-Shapes.mkv: A lecture recording on object-oriented programming, focusing on class inheritance and implementation for geometric shapes such as circles, regular polygons, squares, and triangles. | 3-Bear.webm: A lecture walkthrough for the 'bear problem' in object-oriented programming, focusing on class inheritance, method overriding, and code reuse with custom bear classes.
